problem: Given the ellipsoid $\frac{(x-1)^{2}}{16}+\frac{{y}^{2}}{4}+(z+2)^{2}=1$, find the domain of $z=z(x,y).$
worked_solution:
From the ellipsoid equation, we make $z$ the subject as follows:

$$
\begin{aligned}\frac{(x-1)^{2}}{16}+\frac{{y}^{2}}{4}+(z+2)^{2} & =1 \\ (z+2)^{2} & =1-\frac{(x-1)^{2}}{16}-\frac{{y}^{2}}{4} \\ z+2 & =\pm \sqrt{1-\frac{(x-1)^{2}}{16}-\frac{{y}^{2}}{4}}\end{aligned}
$$

Since the square root is defined only for non-negative arguments, we have:

$$
\begin{aligned}1-\frac{(x-1)^{2}}{16}-\frac{{y}^{2}}{4}\ge 0 \\ \frac{(x-1)^{2}}{16}+\frac{{y}^{2}}{4}\le 1\end{aligned}
$$

which gives the interior of the ellipse $\frac{(x-1)^{2}}{16}+\frac{{y}^{2}}{4}=1$ and its boundary.

Therefore, the domain is 

$$
{(x,y)\,:\,\frac{(x-1)^{2}}{16}+\frac{{y}^{2}}{4}\le 1}.
$$
